name: AgentLane
summary: Give your AI agent a separate visual workspace in your logged-in Chrome. Requires the local AgentLane bridge and an MCP client.
singlePurpose: Provide a user-directed visual browser workspace for an MCP-compatible AI client in a separate window of the user's existing Chrome profile, using screenshots and tab-targeted input without sharing the physical keyboard or mouse.

permissions.debugger: Required to capture the owned tab's rendered pixels and deliver coordinate clicks, text, scrolling and restricted keys through chrome.debugger. It also configures the viewport, intercepts file choosers and renders standard select menus inside the page to reduce native-window interference. Fixed packaged code performs these operations only on tabs created for that MCP connection and their child frames. The MCP interface exposes no human-tab selection, cookie extraction or arbitrary JavaScript/CDP commands. Debugger access is broad at Chrome's permission level and is disclosed in setup and the security model. All extension logic, including the fixed isolated-world picker bootstrap, is bundled in the ZIP; native requests contain tool data, never executable scripts.
permissions.nativeMessaging: Required to connect the extension to org.agentlane.browser, a separately installed local Node.js native messaging host. It relays requests/results between the extension and a locally running MCP client over an owner-only Unix socket. It does not open a remote-debugging TCP port. Store installation alone does not install this helper or the MCP server. Source and reviewer installation instructions are provided on the project website.
permissions.storage: Required to persist the user-selected starting-website policy and accepted screenshot/input disclosure version in chrome.storage.local. Selected websites and explicit Any website modes remain distinct. No browsing history, screenshot history or analytics are stored in extension storage.

remoteCodeExplanation: All extension logic, including the fixed isolated-world select presentation bootstrap, is included in the ZIP. Native messages contain requests for a fixed set of tool operations, never executable scripts or CDP methods. The separate native host and MCP server are source-available local software. Pages visited by the user-directed workflow load their own normal site resources; these are not remotely hosted extension logic.

dataHandling.websiteContent: Screenshots of the owned tab can contain visible site content, forms and documents.
dataHandling.userActivity: The local bridge handles requested clicks, scrolls, keys and text for the user-directed task, not physical desktop input monitoring.
dataHandling.webHistory: Requested URLs and visible page addresses are handled for the owned task. General browsing history is not read.
dataHandling.sensitiveCategories: Visible screenshots and user-directed text may contain personally identifiable information, personal communications, authentication information, financial/payment information, health information and location information. The pipeline does not redact or classify these pixels, so disclose these potential categories rather than claiming they cannot be handled. No cookie/password-store extraction API is exposed.
dataHandling.recipients: The user's local MCP client and any AI/model providers it is configured to use; websites receive normal browsing and submitted actions. No developer-hosted collection/analytics/model endpoint is operated by this extension.
